ch01.alt: A black-and-white photograph of a crowd of men in caps and tunics massed in a courtyard before a two-story building, a broad white banner or awning stretched overhead; a few figures in the foreground carry staves.
ch01.caption: The Shanghai Workers' Pickets before the general headquarters of the third armed uprising, March 1927.

ch01.before: Just as the Shanghai workers were celebrating
ch01.alt: A black-and-white photograph of a long file of workers in caps and dark tunics marching down a city street lined with onlookers.
ch01.caption: The Shanghai Workers' Pickets setting out to join a citizens' rally, 27 March 1927.

ch02.before: Mainly, though, Section One set up various working offices
ch02.alt: A black-and-white photograph looking down a narrow brick lane at the doorway and upper-floor bay window of a shikumen terraced house in the former French Concession.
ch02.caption: The former site of the Central Military Commission's offices during Zhou Enlai's time as its secretary in Shanghai: Lafayette Lane, off Rue Lafayette in the former French Concession (now 553 Central Fuxing Road).

ch02.before: At first the Standing Committee of the Central Political Bureau
ch02.alt: A grainy black-and-white photograph of a Shanghai street frontage: a shopfront hung with Chinese signboards, and a period automobile parked at the curb with two men beside it.
ch02.caption: The former site of the CCP Central Political Bureau's offices in Shanghai, 1928–1931: 477 Yunnan Road (now 171–173 Yunnan Central Road). [The building number is given as 447 in the text of this chapter and as 477 on this photograph in the source; both are reproduced as printed.]

ch03.before: Chen Geng, Zhou Yiqun, and Lu Dongsheng left Shantou
ch03.alt: A worn black-and-white photograph of a young woman holding a small boy of two or three against her side; both look off to one side.
ch03.caption: Wang Genying and Chen Zhifei, Shanghai, 1931.
